A structural gravity assessment of Donald Trump's 2025 tariff agenda and what
it means for the UK. We simulate six scenarios, ranging from targeted US
tariffs to full global retaliation.

## Key findings

- Full-scale trade conflict produces a **$1.4 trillion global welfare loss**.
- Trade diversion can briefly favour the UK: in one scenario **UK exports to
  the US rise by 17.5%**.
- Under full retaliation, **UK exports to the US fall by 43.6%**.
- Imports shrink across the board, threatening input supplies for sectors
  such as aerospace and technology.
- As in the 2018 US–China trade war, escalation brings higher prices, weaker
  competitiveness and fragmented supply chains — no economy emerges unscathed.

## Policy recommendations

Adapt global value chains by diversifying suppliers; diversify trade through
CPTPP and a deal with India; keep trade policy agile while strengthening
multilateral cooperation; and stabilise the relationship with the EU through
sector-specific deals, lower non-tariff barriers, digitised customs,
regulatory alignment and investment in trade infrastructure.

For how these numbers played out once the tariffs landed, see the
[Trump Trade War Diary — Day 189](/blog/2025-07-27-trump-trade-war-diary-day-189/index.qmd)
and the peer-reviewed follow-up,
[The Return of Protectionism](return-of-protectionism-trump-tariffs.qmd).

**Report:** Centre for Business Prosperity, Aston University, March 2025.
With Jun Du.
